leted unread — one click to jump in.
# dsh-session-dashboard
A DeepSeek Harness Web GUI plugin: an **always-visible session status card in the left sidebar** (ab
ove Settings), so recent session activity is visible without opening a page.
English | 中文
## Features
- Persistent card in the left sidebar; when the sidebar collapses to its 56px rail it becomes an ico

n button with a "Needs you" badge
- One row per session: status glyph, title, current activity (Wait

ing for approval / Working / Completed unread / Idle) and relative time
- Filters All / Needs you /

Running / Done with live counts; the card keeps the same height when switching filters
- Click a row

to open that session; `+` starts a new session
- The currently open session has a tinted background

and bold title; the highlight follows session navigation
- Click the card header (disclosure caret)
to collapse or expand it; the collapsed header keeps the current status counts, and the state is re

membered in this browser
- 5 rows by default, expandable to 10
- Settings → Sessions card section: c

ard language (English / 中文) and default row count
- Needs-you, running and unread-completed sessions
are listed first; running rows have a sweep animation
> Session titles in the screenshot are sample data.
Verified on DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (Web profile) and `0.2.1-rc.3` (Desktop profile): installed with the of
ficial `dsh plugin` command, `--dump-config` shows the `# == dsh-session-dashboard` layer, client-mo
dules serves the bundle, card placement/filters/navigation/new-session/rail badge all work, and the
console reports no plugin errors.
## Official plugin form
This is a standard DSH **bundle**, not a private extension of the host:
| Official requirement | This package |
| `dsh.bundle.patch` points at the config layer | `./cordis.patch.yml` inserts the package into the

Loader by name |
| `dsh.client.platform: "web"` + `exports["./client"]` | points at `client/client.j

s` (prebuilt `__ModuleLoader__` factory) |
| `engines.dsh` compatibility range | `>=0.2.0 <0.3.0` (p

asses on 0.2.1-rc.2 / rc.3) |
| Installed into the profile's `bundles` list | `dsh plugin add` appen

ds it automatically |
| Prebuilt artifact, no install-time build | plain JS, no `prepare`/build scri

pt, so git/tarball/npm installs need no build approval |
| `license`, `icon`, `files` | MIT, `icon.s
vg`, complete publish file list |
Official docs: Package and install a plugin.
## Install
The plugin is browser-only: no Host service, no configuration, no background work. Install and unins
tall go through the official `dsh plugin` command (pnpm + profile manifest); no hand-edited profile
the official `dsh plugin` command (pnpm + profile manifest); no hand-edited profile or node_modules.

### 3. Web profile

`dsh plugin` resolves the local package as a pnpm `link:` dependency and appends the bundle automati
cally; restart `dsh web` (or refresh the page) to apply.
## Data sources
The card requests nothing from the Host and stores no session state. It occupies the root-scoped sid
ebar footer seat and reads the standard seats the slot system provides to every root slot:
| Seat / data | Used for |
| `useSessions` | session catalog, `displayTitle`, `updatedAt`, `blank`/`origin`, `projectionsBySess

ion` |
| `useSessionStatus` | `running`, `pendingInteraction` (`approval` / `plan-review` / `questio

n`), `completionUnread` |
| `useWorkspaces` | `archivedSessionIds` (archived sessions are hidden by

default) |
| `projectionsBySession[*].values` | `todos` (current todo), `turnOutline` (current promp
t and turn count), `sessionStats` |
Opening a session uses `ctx.uiWorkspace.openSession(id)`, starting one uses `ctx.uiWorkspace.startSe
ssion()`, and the collapsed-rail icon uses `ctx.layout.toggleSidebar()`.
## Structure
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`client/client.js` is a hand-written CJS-in-loader factory (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, fact
ory })`) and **needs no build**: edit it and refresh. Its only runtime dependency is `react` from th
e platform baseline; styling uses the host's `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens, so light and dark themes
baseline; styling uses the host's `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens, so light and dark themes both work.
Known limitations: docs/limitations.md.
